A1.justification: Both PDFs describe HATEDAY and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E. Corresponding content can be reliably matched despite rewriting and layout changes.

before.justification: V1 reports original tweet annotation, hate-speech prevalence analyses, detector evaluations, and error and moderation analyses, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original dataset analyses and detector evaluations, including the empirical results and confidence intervals in Tables 2–3 and 5–6.

M1.justification: The detector architectures, zero-shot prompt, inference procedures, and construction of hatefulness scores remain unchanged in Section 3.1 and Appendix D. No new detection algorithm or model component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 240,000-tweet dataset covering eight languages and four countries, the same academic dataset supersets, and HateCheck for six languages. No evaluated task, population, or domain is added.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 and 5–6 and Appendix D.1 retain the same supervised classifiers, Perspective API, Aya23 8B, and Llama3.1 8B in their corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 2.2 removes v1's expert-and-annotator re-examination of tweets with any hateful vote or no majority; v2 states only simple majority voting. This revises the reported annotation protocol, without establishing that labels or experiments were recomputed. Other evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.2 reduces the qualitative false-positive evidence by removing several illustrative tweets, including the Portuguese slang example and its explanation. The quantitative error, target-alignment, and moderation analyses remain unchanged, including the appendix plots.

E5.justification: Both versions report 95% bootstrapped confidence intervals in Tables 5–6, three prompt runs per tweet in Appendix D.2, and the same t-test and correlation statistics. No uncertainty-reporting procedure or repeated-run information is added.

E6.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported mean average precision from 36.0% to 41.1% for the best open-source models and from 39.1% to 44.3% for Perspective. The zero-shot summary switches from Llama3.1 at 28.4% to Aya23 at 32.4%. Tables 2–3 and 5–6 retain their scores; these are aggregate-reporting revisions, not demonstrated model improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix E.3 retains the same predicted-positive identities and derivation of the review fraction, S = recall × base rate / precision. No mathematical assumptions, definitions, proofs, or theoretical results are substantively revised.

C1.justification: The dataset novelty and poor real-world detection claims remain. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion replace categorical claims that human-in-the-loop moderation is unfeasible or prohibitively costly with the qualified claim that high moderation coverage requires substantial human review.

C2.justification: Section 5 adds conceptual alignment as a possible explanation for the Nigerian classifier's advantage and elaborates explanations for English/US–India performance gaps. The limitations newly acknowledge untested prompt choices, while the moderation discussion adopts more conditional feasibility conclusions.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies Perspective's Identity Attack attribute and that target annotations use free-text labels. Appendix B.2 replaces the anonymous annotation-guidelines link with a named GitHub link. Hardware, model sizes, prompts, and hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged; the adjudication description is removed.

R1.justification: The discussion adds contextual references, including Nozza (2021), Haber et al. (2023), Hartmann et al. (2025), and Ye et al. (2023), while removing Vidgen et al. (2019). These broaden connections to prior research without substantially redefining the work's novelty or positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, substantial portions of the results and discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Revised headings and additional paragraph divisions clarify the narrative, including Reasons for Low Performance and Target alignment and performance. These language changes extend well beyond the added scientific qualifications.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn as a dataset-and-findings schematic, Figure 7 is enlarged to span both columns, and Table 1 moves columns and relabels Origin as Split. Other empirical displays retain their content, with limited caption and formatting changes.

improvement.justification: V2's qualified moderation conclusion better matches the unchanged cost–recall evidence than v1's blanket infeasibility claim. Clearer writing, additional evaluation details, and the prompt limitation provide further modest benefits. However, removing the expert-adjudication description leaves the annotation procedure less transparent. Overall, the revision improves the paper modestly while retaining essentially the same empirical evidence.
